title: Lexicographic Height-Balanced Binary Search Trees for Chronos-Topology Maps in Haskell
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a purely functional implementation of a lexicographically ordered binary search tree that serves as the core indexing structure for Chronos-Topology maps. The tree preserves a strict height-balanced invariant, guaranteeing $O(\log N)$ point and range queries, as well as $O(\log N)$ insertions and deletions. We formally prove that the tree maintains key ordering and height balance after each update. Static abstract-syntax-tree inspection confirms a structural complexity of 150 SLOC and a single function block. No empirical timing measurements are reported; the analysis relies solely on static reasoning and formal proofs. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/haskell-functional-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261113_230131_data_structures_in_aether-cont}
